title: Recover decisive verification evidence after large or cleaned-up output

intentCoverage.report:
**Dough Intent Coverage verdict: Caught.** The maintained timing assertion still catches loss of a completed proof command's active-time exclusion after its change to partial equality. This verdict covers the observed completed-run path only.

Source: `SEED-345#recover-decisive-verification-evidence`, `.planning/seeds/SEED-345-session-token-efficiency.md#recover-decisive-verification-evidence`, and completed plan `.planning/slice-plans/683-recover-decisive-verification-evidence/PLAN.md`, at revision `45ff02fee774a270826cd7507fee2ce1c9d077cc`. Slice 1 explicitly retains `slice-clock.test.mjs` as timing and lifecycle regression proof while adding recoverable run evidence. The supplied promise, fault family, fixture and focused command were confirmed against that revision.

The promise checked was that six active minutes, a nine-minute command through `run`, and four more active minutes report ten active minutes, while the command's output and successful status remain recoverable. Exactly one temporary fault changed `Distribution/src/skills/dough-execute-plan/scripts/slice-clock-run.mjs:75` from `command.endedAt ??= now` to `command.endedAt ??= command.startedAt`, collapsing each completed command's excluded interval to zero. Fixtures and maintained assertions stayed intact.

The maintained focused command was `env PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH bash scripts/test.sh Distribution/tests/skills/dough-execute-plan/slice-clock.test.mjs`, run from the scratch checkout through its installed slice-clock `run`, with separate logs, exit files, runner timing files and case outcomes for each phase. Node was v24.21.0 and Bash was 5.3.20. The scratch checkout received its own current-lockfile installation through `node scripts/setup-native.mjs npm`; no dependency copy or symlink was used.

- Baseline: exit 0; all eight cases passed.
- Faulted: exit 1; five cases passed and three timing cases failed. The selected actual catch was `Distribution/tests/skills/dough-execute-plan/slice-clock.test.mjs:48`: `assert.partialDeepStrictEqual(ran.result, reported("run", "running", 6))`. Its failure showed 15 elapsed minutes instead of 6, zero remaining instead of 9, and a false overrun. This is the changed assertion itself, rather than an earlier helper. The overlapping-command and nonzero-command cases also failed; they were not additional faults or separate probes.
- Independent wrong-behavior observation: a separate scratch program reused the real CLI and `Distribution/tests/support/slice-clock-fixture.mjs` controlled clock. It moved the clock from minute 0 to 6, ran the command through minute 15, and queried status at minute 19. Arithmetic independent of the implementation gives 6 + 4 = 10 active minutes and 9 excluded minutes. The faulted CLI instead returned 15 elapsed immediately after `run` and 19 at status. The observed clock record had equal command start/end timestamps, while the run-evidence record separately retained a nine-minute start/end interval and exit status 0. The log still contained `suite passed\nwarned\n`, and the exit file contained `0\n`. Thus the intended completed-run transition was reached and its timing went wrong while output and exit evidence succeeded.
- Restoration: a finally handler restored the original source bytes; signal handlers also arranged restoration. Byte equality was confirmed, `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` was empty, and the same focused command then exited 0 with all eight cases passing. HEAD remained the selected revision.

The owned scratch workspace was `/Users/terryyin/git/open-dough/.worktrees/intent-coverage-683-run-interval-20261117`, branch `codex/intent-coverage-683-run-interval-20261117`, created at the selected revision from originating checkout `/Users/terryyin/git/open-dough/.worktrees/recover-decisive-verification-evidence-after-lar`. After the restored pass, its clean worktree and branch were removed without force. The scratch path, Git registration, branch, temporary witness, logs and evidence directory were verified absent. The originating checkout remained clean at the selected revision. No primary-checkout edit, commit, push, backlog change or CI observer action was made.

**Next proof action:** accept the existing focused timing proof for this completed-command exclusion fault; no assertion repair is indicated by this probe. The caller owns broader review and follow-up routing.

**Prior disposition:** the completed plan already records no product correction and evaluation on the next real planned execution after release. This result supports retaining that disposition; it creates no new repair decision and does not replace that evaluation.

- **Test runtime.** 6.4 seconds total (measured from the maintained runner's timing files): baseline 2.2 s, faulted 2.1 s, restored 2.1 s. Setup and the independent witness are outside these runner figures.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable in minutes: no separate human-time measure was supplied. Zero human interventions were observed during the check.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable in tokens or currency: this host exposed no separate per-agent usage measure. Invocation elapsed is not substituted for effort.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 271913 ms (measured), from 1794935677000 to 1794935948913 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

Wrap-up disposition: 45ff02fee774a270826cd7507fee2ce1c9d077cc — Caught; retain the existing completed-run timing proof, no follow-up.
